title: Review of c46's dt/2 check: Supported. On fresh seed 17 (128^2) halving the world's step leaves the prey-predator curves within one body of the dt 0.2 run and gives the same predator divisions (6 vs 6 persistent splits, generation 2)
summary: Ran the claim's world (dt 0.2) and the finding's world (dt 0.1, 1000 steps per frame) on seed 17, 128^2, t=12000, --lineage-k 5. Prey every 1000 t: 5/13/15/1/6/18/18/12/8/4/4/3/4 (dt 0.2) vs 5/13/15/1/6/18/19/13/8/4/5/3/3 (dt 0.1); predators 0/0/0/15/15/15/11/11/12/11/5/8/9 vs 0/0/0/15/15/15/11/11/12/11/6/9/9. Predator persistent splits 6 and 6 (generation 2 in both), 8 splits each; prey persistent splits 1 and 0. One lagged swing in both, the prey dwindling to 3-4 by t=12000.

observations.D: dthalf_s17/lineage.png: 6 predator persistent splits, generation 2, as base_s17
observations.X: dthalf_s17 vs base_s17 metrics: prey and predator counts agree within one body at every 1000 t

verdicts.limitation: 128^2 and one fresh seed; at this size the prey nearly die out by t=12000 on seed 17 in both arms, so the check covers one swing. No grid-spacing variant. I did not rerun the finding's g screen.
